findings.summary: Call completion and its lifecycle transition are not recoverable as one logical operation. finish_goal_call persists RECORD_CALL_RESULT before persisting the resulting mode. If a graceful stop has recorded MODE_STOPPING and interruption occurs after the call-result append but before _set_mode(MODE_STOPPED), restore clears the completed call yet retains MODE_STOPPING. There is then no in-flight call to drain, no pending execution to finish the transition, and next_goal_call refuses admission indefinitely unless explicitly resumed. The completed call result also contains the terminal intent, but restore never applies it when the separate mode record is missing. Derive the missing completion transition during reconstruction or persist completion and its resulting lifecycle state together. Add an isolated regression interrupting between the completion record and mode persistence, including graceful-stop drainage. This violates behavior 5 and P6's journal-based recovery requirement and requires no live Runtime testing.
